summary: CKGSB's marketing team is juggling the Knowledge website redesign, the launch of the Intelligent China program, and final preparations for the Women in Leadership Forum, while resolving an email lockout and aligning global search strategy around Asia Star and Intelligent China.
summaryDetail: The Knowledge website redesign is at a critical feedback stage: Joseph must share the HTML design concept, and a 30-minute session with Julie and the team lead is needed to mark specific feedback before Joker makes changes; the launch also requires adding more publication news and aligning the She Innovates design. The Intelligent China webpage is ready to launch and drive traffic, but Joseph still needs to draft target areas/prompts and analyze Asia Star participant profiles and CRM hot leads to sharpen audience focus. For the upcoming Women in Leadership Forum, Alan Chen must put up banners and brochures using the previous version, while Joseph needs to replace the homepage screenshot in the PPT with the final version and hyperlink mentioned sites, and publish the MBZUAI article with the revised caption (LIU Xuan to check for a better photo of the gifting moment). This week, the team must resolve the Outlook account lockout by updating credentials on all devices and contacting JSB to confirm backend unlock. Looking ahead, Ira Zaka has several November deadlines: confirming the English translation of Professor Jon Liao's obituary, editing the school women's figures with the latest data, and reviewing the YouTube channel enhancement document; also, Joseph must obtain a brief on conversion tracking setup from the SEO manager to improve Google Ads tracking documentation.

decisions.text: Stale saved passwords across devices caused the account lockout; all devices must update credentials.
Remove the standalone videos section; videos will be dispersed by topic instead.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge menu and School menu).
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner.
Do not display a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs; Berkeley as optional third; hold US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) for now.
Include Berkeley program in the audit phase consideration.
Use the revised caption: 'Dean Xiang Bing (left) with Liang Hong, Vice President of MBZUAI and CKGSB EMBA Alumna (right).'
